name: Sketch
description:
Sketch is a macOS design tool for creating interfaces, vector graphics, component libraries, prototypes, and developer handoff material. It keeps the main editing experience native and local while adding web-based collaboration when a project needs it.

Design screens on an infinite canvas, build reusable components, connect screens into a prototype, then share the relevant work with teammates or developers. It is particularly useful for product designers who want a focused Mac editor without making the browser the center of their craft.

Sketch works offline, but shared workspaces and handoff add a broader collaboration layer. The best fit is a design team that agrees on its library and sharing workflow; importing a tool alone does not create consistency in a product system.

## Features

- Create interface and vector work with frames, stack layouts, components, templates, and shared libraries.
- Work locally and offline in the macOS editor, which currently requires macOS Sonoma or later.
- Build interactive prototypes with overlays, scrolling areas, hover, press, drag, and swipe interactions.
- Co-edit in real time or share selected documents and password-protected previews for feedback.
- Let developers inspect files, download assets, and export design tokens through the free handoff tools.

## Where it fits

Sketch fits Mac-based product and interface designers who value a focused native editor and a mature component workflow. It can support individual exploration through to team review and developer handoff.

It is not a general image editor or a substitute for design-system governance. Teams should confirm compatibility and collaboration needs before standardizing on it.
